LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard source URLs pointing to GitHub releases for the package, using HTTPS and pinned version tags. The `source` array entries fetch prebuilt binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 from the official GitHub repository of the project, which is consistent with typical binary package practices. The checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the sourcing process when `makepkg` parses the file.

There is no top-level code execution, command substitution, or `pkgver()` function that would execute arbitrary commands during sourcing. The variables are simple string assignments or array definitions, with no signs of obfuscation, dynamic code evaluation (e.g., `eval`, `base64`, `curl|bash`), or data exfiltration attempts. The `pkgver` is hardcoded, so no network operations occur during version resolution.

Since `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` only sources the PKGBUILD and downloads the sources without running `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`, and since no malicious execution occurs during sourcing or source fetching, this step is safe.
</details>

The .SRCINFO file is a metadata file used by Arch User Repository (AUR) packages to describe package properties and sources. It does not contain executable code. The sources are correctly specified as GitHub release binaries for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, hosted at the official project URL (https://github.com/padovanl/portop). The checksums (sha256sums) are provided and match the expected values for the respective binaries. There are no signs of obfuscation, unexpected network operations, or malicious behavior in this metadata file. The use of prebuilt binaries is standard for -bin packages, and checksums are present, enhancing trust in the integrity of the downloads.

The package metadata includes standard fields such as pkgdesc, url, license, and architecture support, all consistent with the project's stated purpose. There are no scripts or commands in this file, and it serves only to inform the AUR build system about the package structure. As such, it poses no security risk.

The source URLs are constructed using the package version and architecture in a predictable and transparent manner, pointing directly to release assets under the declared upstream repository (https://github.com/padovanl/portop).
